newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Rains fall across Kansas.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Rains fall across Kansas.

text.p: Rains fell overnight across a large part of Kansas, and dealers said the moisture would likely halt cutting Wednesday in the northwest part of the state.

"Rain in northwest Kansas should slow things down for a few hours today. It will actually be a nice breather and give (grain dealers and farmers) a chance to get caught up. We'll be able to move some wheat and clear some storage space," a south central Kansas dealer said.
Heavy rain and large hail hit south central and southeast Kansas overnight, but dealers said they were not concerned.

"We got dime- and quarter-sized hail and then about 1-1/2 to two inches of rain. I don't think anyone's too concerned because we're pretty much done with harvest, and the rain was really needed," the dealer said.
Farmer-selling was slow Tuesday, and another Kansas dealer blamed the slow movement on wheat prices, which are hovering around three-year lows.
Meanwhile, basis bids were mostly unchanged Wednesday, although bids at the Gulf of Mexico were slightly firmer.
